packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-03 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: no identification or prior reading of this material was
present in my context. I did not identify the work or author.

Beyond-rules disclosure: in addition to viewing the original images, I made
contrast-enhanced, 2x-upscaled crops of the tile images (scratch folder
b17/enh03, derived only from this packet's images) and viewed three of them
(from image-002 and image-003). They were not more legible than the originals,
so all readings below are from the original images. I opened nothing else.

All 25 images loaded.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Five overviews: image-001, -006, -011, -016, -021, each followed by four
  native-resolution tiles (002-005, 007-010, 012-015, 017-020, 022-025).
- Each overview shows a long, narrow parchment strip (a binding strip or guard)
  laid horizontally across a paper leaf, with a thin rod or thread crossing it
  lengthwise. Only 2 to 4 written lines survive per text block. Upper and lower
  lines are cut through horizontally.
- Each strip shows four text blocks, separated by ruled vertical bounding lines
  and blank margins. Read as two blocks on the left (A, B) and two on the right
  (C, D), with a wide blank area between B and C. This looks like two columns
  per page, or an opening, seen across a fold, but the crop is too narrow to
  confirm it. I cannot tell which block comes first in reading order beyond
  left to right.
- Script: small Gothic book hand, brown ink, many abbreviations. Dry-point or
  plummet ruling is visible.
- Face 1 (image-004, block D): a larger "R" with a crossed stroke begins a line
  (it could be a response sign or a capital). No rubrics or colour can be seen.
  No glosses or marginalia can be seen. On face 1 the ink is faint and the
  writing looks partly mirrored or offset. It may be seen through the strip
  from the other side; treat face 1 readings as least reliable.
- Overlaps: image-002 and -003 share block B's left edge, image-003 and -004
  share block C's left edge, and image-004 and -005 share block D. The same
  pattern holds on every face. Repeated words in an overlap are not counted twice.

Line numbers count the lines visible on that tile from the top, including the
cut partial line at the top when it exists.

======================================================================
FACE 1 (overview image-001)
Block A - image-002
 002 l1  [top half of line cut; illegible]
 002 l2  ue(l)? s(e)c(un)d(u)m(?) [illegible] sit longitudi(n)e(?)
 002 l3  de luce(?) dicam(us)?(?) sit(?) [illegible] forma(?)
 002 l4  [bottom-cut; illegible]
Block B - image-003
 003 l1  [top-cut] [illegible] ... in(?) [illegible]
 003 l2  m(u)lt(?)a  [..]he[..]m(?) in [..]ano(?) p[..]la(?)
 003 l3  [bottom-cut; illegible]
Block C - image-004
 004 l1  q(ue)?(?) uenit(?) p(er)egrina(?) aliq(ui)s(?)
 004 l2  [..]ltro(?) adiutori(?) uidetur(?) h(?)ic(?)
Block D - image-004 / image-005
 005 l1  R(?) si(?) [..]uit(?) [h?]enomen(?) [illegible]
 005 l2  [illegible: 4-5 words, faint]
Face 1 is essentially unread. The ink is faint, possibly seen through the strip.

======================================================================

Block C - image-009

Face 2 is the most legible face. Its words are still mostly uncertain.

FACE 5 (overview image-021)
Block A - image-022
 022 l1  rite(?) namq(ue) n(on) solu(m)(?)/ n(on)(?) e(ss)e(?) sollicita(?) a[..]
 022 l2  [fold] [..] ab(?) [..] nu(n)c(?) n(on) (est)(?) h(oc)(?)

Block B - image-023

 023 l3  dic(tu)m(?)/ diam(?) (et) eccl(esi)am(?) expectatio(n)e(m)(?) synag(og)e(?)
Block C - image-024
 024 l1  [top-cut] [..] clamen(?) [..] [..] exe(m)plum(?)
 024 l2  sed(?)a(m)(?) [..] (con)uult(?) belliuos(?)/ bellicos(?) in[..]
 024 l3  [fold] [..]one(?) uel(?) [..] [..]
 024 l4  [bottom-cut] [..] enormis(?) uenit(?)
Block D - image-025
 025 l1  aiussa(?)/ ad(?)iuss(?) p(ro)posito(?) m(?)is(?) s(e)ntentiis(?) c(on)
 025 l2  [fold; illegible]
 025 l3  uerente(?) fortissi(m)e(?) s[..]imon(?) filio tue(?)
 025 l4  [bottom-cut; illegible]

======================================================================
SELECTION AND UNREAD AREAS
- I attempted every block on every face. These strips are not suitable for
  connected spans of ten or more lines. At most 2 to 4 lines exist per block,
  and the top and bottom lines of each are cut through. The middle line on
  several faces is hidden by a fold or the crossing rod.
- Unread: all cut top and bottom lines, the lines under the folds, and nearly
  all of face 1 (faint ink, possibly reversed).
- The best material for any later source match: face 2 (blocks A, C, D),
  face 3 (blocks A, B), face 4 (block B) and face 5 (blocks B, D). Even these
  readings are tentative, word by word.
- Suggested follow-up: imaging under raking or transmitted light, or images
  with the strip lifted or the rod removed. A higher-resolution image of
  face 1 is also needed.

LIMITATIONS
- This is an unverified image reading. Most words carry a question mark, and
  expansions are proposals. I did not supply words from sense.
- The column and page order across the fold is uncertain. Blocks C and D may
  belong to a different page from A and B.
